title: Feedback Stabilization of Switched Systems: Memory is not needed
summary: A long-standing assumption in the literature on switched linear systems is that static, homogeneous of degree one feedbacks form the most general class of controllers necessary and sufficient for stabilization. In this paper, we provide a rigorous justification. More specifically, we prove by construction that if a switched linear system admits a stabilizing full-information controller, with access to the entire history of states and switching signals, then a memoryless and homogeneous of degree one stabilizing controller also exists.
